title: Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution in the commuting operator framework
authors: Gereon Koßmann, René Schwonnek, Po-Chieh Liu, Hao-Chung Cheng
abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD) is arguably the gold standard for secure quantum communication, as it aims to rely only on observed input-output statistics of an uncharacterized device which is only assumption to obey the laws of quantum physics. A corresponding security analysis hence demands a description of a quantum experiment from a most general perspective. Under close inspection, existing proof techniques do not always meet this goal as they tend to rely on subtile assumptions on a tensor product structure of the underlying Hilbert space and a 'hidden but finite' dimensionality. In this work, we collect the tools needed for a full analysis of DIQKD in the commuting operator framework, which avoids these subtilities and provides the arguably most general view on a quantum experiment. We rigorously proof the common assumption that in DIQKD measurements can be w.l.o.g. assumed to be projective. Furthermore, we show that task of computing key rates can be casted as a non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problem to which the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy gives a correct and converging relaxation.   As a tool, we generalize the integral representation for the relative entropy by Frenkel [Quantum 7, 1102 (2023)] to general von Neumann algebras and apply techniques from Kossmann and Schwonnek [arXiv: 2411.04858] for the approximation in an NPO program.
summary: This paper establishes a highly general mathematical framework for analyzing Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (DIQKD) using commuting operators. It overcomes limitations in previous work by employing advanced tools from operator algebras to handle arbitrary environments. The result provides rigorous security bounds by casting the key rate calculation into a solvable Non-Commutative Polynomial Optimization problem.
main_problem: To develop a maximally general mathematical framework for analyzing Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (DIQKD) security that avoids restrictive assumptions on the underlying Hilbert space structure.
main_result: The authors provide a representation-independent route to derive AEP-based security statements by utilizing the commuting operator framework, proving key results like the projectivity of measurements w.l.o.g.
method: The work employs advanced tools from operator algebras (C*-algebras, von Neumann algebras) and casts the key rate computation as a Non-Commutative Polynomial Optimization (NPO) problem solvable via the NPA hierarchy.
model_or_system: The system is DIQKD involving two parties (Alice and Bob). The mathematical model uses universal C*-algebras to represent local measurements, allowing for rigorous analysis of security even when Eve's side information requires general von Neumann algebras.
key_observables: Key rates, conditional von Neumann entropy, observed input-output statistics ($ho_{AB}$)
important_parameters: The framework is designed to be general regarding the structure of the underlying Hilbert space and environment description (e.g., type-III algebra for Eve).
main_assumptions: It addresses and overcomes limitations in existing proofs that rely on specific tensor product structures or assume measurements are always projective.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general DIQKD experimental setup involving local Random Number Generators (RNGs) used by Alice and Bob to generate output statistics.
paper_structure: The paper builds from reviewing necessary algebraic concepts (C*-algebras, states, traces) before detailing the DIQKD formulation in Section 5. It introduces technical tools like generalized relative entropy formulas for von Neumann algebras and applies these to the NPO problem.
why_interesting: It pushes the boundaries of quantum information theory by providing security proofs that are robust against uncharacterized devices and complex environmental interactions, which is crucial for realizing practical quantum technologies.

figures.caption: Figure 1. The figure illustrates a device-independent quantum key distribution (DIQKD) experiment. In contrast to the quantum game depicted in Figure 2, the referee is replaced by local random number generators (RNGs), one on each side. While sharing a quantum state ρAB, Alice and Bob use their respective RNGs to draw private and local random inputs, feed them into their devices, and collect the resulting output statistics.

Figure 2. The figure illustrates a non-local quantum game. A source prepares a bipartite state ρAB and distributes it between Alice and Bob. Following a predetermined strategy, specified by the shared state together with their local measurements, Alice and Bob receive questions x ∈X and y ∈Y from a referee, feed them as inputs into their respective devices, and respond with the outcomes a ∈A and b ∈B produced by their local boxes.
